apps/desktop/src/components/ui/select.ts.content: Dead code / no-op branch. `position === "popper" && ""` always evaluates to either `""` (when popper) or `false`, both of which are ignored by `cn()`, so this argument never contributes any class. It appears to be a leftover placeholder where the intended popper styles were meant to go. Remove it, or replace it with the actual classes intended for the popper position.

apps/desktop/src/components/ui/toggle-gr.content: `style` (and `data-variant`/`data-size`/`data-spacing`/`data-orientation`) are assigned before `{...props}` is spread, and React does not merge two `style` props — the last one wins. A caller passing any `style` silently drops `--gap`, after which `gap-[--spacing(var(--gap))]` resolves to `calc(var(--spacing) * <missing>)`, an invalid value that falls back to no gap. Similarly, caller-supplied `data-*` attributes desynchronize the `data-[...]`/`group-data-*` selectors from the actual configuration. Merge the caller style (or spread `props` before the derived attributes) to preserve the computed values.

apps/desktop/src/index.html.content:
There is no fallback for a bootstrap failure. If `./app/main.tsx` fails to fetch (transient dev-server error / stale build) or the module throws while evaluating/importing, `#root` stays empty and the Electron window renders completely blank with no visible error — the only trace is the DevTools console, which is not open by default in the packaged app. This makes startup failures silent and hard to diagnose.

Consider adding a minimal fallback/error surface, e.g. an inline `<noscript>`/placeholder is not enough for module failures; a small inline script that listens for `error`/`unhandledrejection` on the window and renders a visible message into `#root` would make failures observable.

docs/finish/evidence/T-PLAN-14/benchmark.content: Evidence artifact lacks reproducibility/provenance fields: there is no code revision (commit SHA), toolchain/node version as a structured value, timestamp, or explicit pass/fail verdict. `machine` and `track` are free-text strings that cannot be machine-verified, and `budgetMs` is present but no boolean/derived field records whether `maxMs` (7.22) actually passed `budgetMs` (2000). Add structured fields (e.g. `commit`, `nodeVersion`, `timestamp`, `passed`) so the result can be tied to a specific build and independently reproduced.

packages/ble/src/index.ts.content: Stale/misleading header. The comment still scopes the package to "backends, scan, link, commands and sim (T-BLE-01 to T-BLE-04)", but this barrel also re-exports modules added in later slices: `./stream.js` (T-BLE-05), `./qualify.js` (T-BLE-06), `./encrypted.js` (T-BLE-07) and `./provisioning.js` (T-BLE-10). packages/cloud/src/index.ts.content: The package's public entrypoint (`index.ts`) is not exercised by any test: `client.test.ts` imports from `./client.js` and `cross-check.test.ts` imports from `./cross-check.js`/`./client.js`, never from `./index.js`. This matters because a value-vs-type misclassification here (e.g. moving a runtime class like `CloudMetadataClient`/`CloudApiError` or a function into the `export type` block) is *not* caught by `tsc` — a class has a type side, so `export type { CloudApiError } from "./client.js"` compiles cleanly but is erased at runtime, producing a runtime/bundler "export not found" for consumers. Consider adding a barrel test that imports every re-exported symbol through the package entrypoint (or a `tsc`-based public-surface assertion) so any future drift fails CI.

packages/govee/src/actions.test.ts.content: The `FakeLamp` construction block (and the matching `ActionFixture` literal passed to `identify`/`testChase`) is copy-pasted almost verbatim across five tests (IDENTIFY stream, armed snap, unarmed colorwc, TEST CHASE, armed ramp). Extracting small factory helpers (e.g. `segmentedLamp(MAC_A, { zones: 4, armSettleMs: 0, answersStatusWhileArmed: false })` and a `fixture(overrides)` builder) removes the repetition and makes future FakeLamp option changes a single edit instead of five.
